experiments.why: Core stats subtype 0 must give the GET_STATS opcode 0x38 followed by 0x00.
A full 32-byte key should give 0x1d followed by exactly those 32 key bytes.
A key that decodes to 2 bytes must be rejected with a 32B error, not zero-padded.
A 33-byte key must throw a 32B error instead of being cut to 32 bytes.
A full 32-byte key should give 0x1b followed by the 32 key bytes.
A short 2-byte key must throw a 32B error.
A 33-byte key passes the caller's length >= 64 guard and must still throw a 32B error.
A full key should give 0x27, three zero bytes, then the 32 key bytes.
A 33-byte key must throw a 32B error rather than be truncated.
Login frame should be 0x1a, the 32 key bytes, then 'pw' with no trailing null.
An empty password should leave only 0x1a and the 32 key bytes.
Trailing non-hex characters after a valid 32-byte prefix must throw a 32B error, not be silently dropped.
Empty anon request data must throw the >=1 byte error after a valid key.
Empty binary request data must throw the >=1 byte error after a valid key.
An empty trace path must throw the >=1 byte error before any bytes are written.
A 3-byte body is shorter than the 4-byte now header and must give null.
A 3-byte body is shorter than the 4-byte now header and must give null.

source.quote: expect(hex(buildGetStats(0x00))).toBe('3800');

obligations.statement: buildGetStats(0x00) returns the two bytes 0x38 0x00: the CMD_GET_STATS opcode followed by the subtype.

source.quote: buildLogout is [0x1d][32B pubkey]

obligations.statement: buildLogout(pubkeyHex) returns the byte 0x1d followed by the 32 bytes of the destination public key.

source.quote: buildSendStatusReq is [0x1b][32B pubkey]

obligations.statement: buildSendStatusReq(pubkeyHex) returns the byte 0x1b followed by the 32 bytes of the recipient public key.

source.quote: buildSendTelemetryReq is [0x27][3 reserved zero bytes][32B pubkey]

obligations.statement: buildSendTelemetryReq(pubkeyHex) returns the byte 0x27, three zero bytes, then the 32 bytes of the recipient public key.

source.quote: buildSendLogin is [0x1a][32B pubkey][ascii password]

obligations.statement: buildSendLogin(pubkeyHex, 'pw') returns the byte 0x1a, the 32 public key bytes, then the ASCII bytes of the password with no trailing null byte.

source.quote: buildSendLogin with an empty (guest) password is [0x1a][32B pubkey] with no password bytes

obligations.statement: buildSendLogin with an empty password returns only the byte 0x1a and the 32 public key bytes.

source.quote: expect(hex(buildSendAnonReq(pk, Buffer.from([0x01])))).toBe(`39${pk}01`);

obligations.statement: buildSendAnonReq(pubkeyHex, data) returns the byte 0x39, the 32 public key bytes, then the data bytes unchanged.

source.quote: expect(() => buildSendAnonReq(pk, Buffer.alloc(0))).toThrow(/≥1 byte/);

obligations.statement: buildSendAnonReq throws an error mentioning '≥1 byte' when the data buffer is empty.

source.quote: expect(hex(buildSendBinaryReq(pk, Buffer.from([0x05])))).toBe(`32${pk}05`);

obligations.statement: buildSendBinaryReq(pubkeyHex, reqData) returns the byte 0x32, the 32 public key bytes, then the request bytes unchanged.

source.quote: expect(() => buildSendBinaryReq(pk, Buffer.alloc(0))).toThrow(/≥1 byte/);

obligations.statement: buildSendBinaryReq throws an error mentioning '≥1 byte' when the request data buffer is empty.

source.quote: rejects pubkeys shorter than 32 bytes

obligations.statement: buildLogout and buildSendStatusReq throw an error mentioning '32B' when the public key hex decodes to fewer than 32 bytes.

source.quote: rejects overlong pubkeys instead of silently truncating to 32 bytes

obligations.statement: buildLogout, buildSendStatusReq and buildSendTelemetryReq throw an error mentioning '32B' for a 33-byte public key instead of truncating it to 32 bytes.

source.quote: rejects malformed hex (trailing garbage) instead of aliasing to the truncated key

obligations.statement: buildSendLogin, buildSendBinaryReq and buildSendAnonReq throw an error mentioning '32B' when the public key hex has trailing non-hex characters, instead of using the valid 32-byte prefix.

source.quote: buildSendTracePath lays out [0x24][tag u32 LE][auth u32 LE][flags u8][path]

obligations.statement: buildSendTracePath({ tag: 1, authCode: 2, flags: 0, path: [0xaa] }) returns 0x24, the tag as u32 little-endian, the auth code as u32 little-endian, the flags byte, then the path bytes (hex 24010000000200000000aa).

source.quote: buildSendTracePath rejects an empty path

obligations.statement: buildSendTracePath throws an error mentioning '≥1 byte' when the path buffer is empty.

source.quote: expect(res).toEqual({ firmwareVersion: '', nodeName: 'Node A', ownerInfo: 'owner notes' });

obligations.statement: For a body of a 4-byte now clock followed by 'Node A\nowner notes\0', parseAnonOwnerInfo returns { firmwareVersion: '', nodeName: 'Node A', ownerInfo: 'owner notes' }.

source.quote: null-trims the owner field (and anything past the terminator)

obligations.statement: parseAnonOwnerInfo cuts the owner text at the first null byte, so 'Node B\nowner\0garbage' yields nodeName 'Node B' and ownerInfo 'owner'.

source.quote: returns null when the body is too short for the `now` header

obligations.statement: parseAnonOwnerInfo returns null for a body shorter than the 4-byte now header.

source.quote: parses now + a signed Temperature series (size 2, /10)

obligations.statement: parseAvgMinMax reads the leading u32 little-endian now value and decodes a Temperature entry (lpp_type 0x67) as signed 2-byte big-endian values divided by 10, returning { channel, lppType, typeHex, name: 'Temperature', unit: '°C', min, max, avg }.

source.quote: expect(res?.series[0]).toMatchObject({ lppType: 0x75, name: 'Current', unit: 'A', min: 65.535 });

obligations.statement: parseAvgMinMax decodes a Current entry (lpp_type 0x75) as unsigned 2-byte values divided by 1000, so raw 0xffff becomes 65.535 A, not a negative number.

source.quote: returns null on a body too short for "now"

obligations.statement: parseAvgMinMax returns null for a body shorter than the 4-byte now header.

source.quote: stops cleanly on a truncated final entry

obligations.statement: When the last entry is cut short, parseAvgMinMax still returns the now value and leaves that entry out of the series instead of throwing.

source.quote: expect(res?.series[0]).toMatchObject({ name: 'Unknown', min: 10, max: 20, avg: 15 });

obligations.statement: parseAvgMinMax decodes an entry with an unknown lpp_type as 1-byte unscaled values named 'Unknown'.

source.quote: parses two consecutive entries (Temperature then Humidity)

obligations.statement: parseAvgMinMax decodes consecutive entries in order, such as a channel 1 Temperature entry followed by a channel 2 Humidity entry in percent.
